description: What the game compiler refuses, and the message it gives

examples.intent: Script code in a handler

input.natural_language: Run some code when the hero touches a coin
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18">
      <qg:on-collision with="coin">
        score += 1; coin.queue_free()
      </qg:on-collision>
    </qg:character>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: a game is written in tags, not in script

examples.why_invalid: There is no escape hatch: a handler holds actions and q: statements only.
examples.correction: Write <q:set name="score" value="{score + 1}" /> and <qg:destroy /> (score declared with q:set).

examples.intent: A tag the language does not have

input.natural_language: Make the hero fly with a fly tag
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18">
      <qg:fly speed="100" />
    </qg:character>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: Every qg: tag is in the schema; qg:fly is not one of them.
examples.correction: Use controller="behavior" with qg:walk axis="both" (a body without qg:gravity floats).

examples.intent: An attribute the tag does not have

input.natural_language: Give the character a jump power of 300
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18"
                  jump-power="300" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: The message lists the attributes the tag has.
examples.correction: Use jump-speed="300" (pixels per second) or jump-height= (pixels).

examples.intent: A required attribute missing

input.natural_language: Put a character in the scene
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: A character collides by its hitbox, which has no default.
examples.correction: Add hitbox="14x18".

examples.intent: A value not among those an attribute takes

input.natural_language: A character that swims
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="swimmer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: controller= is an enum: platformer, map, topdown, ship, fighter, grid, behavior.
examples.correction: Use controller="platformer" with water tiles (qg:tile kind="water").

examples.intent: A tag in the wrong place

input.natural_language: Put a HUD counter straight in the scene
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:counter bind="score" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: A counter goes inside a qg:hud; the message names where it goes.
examples.correction: Wrap it: <qg:hud><qg:counter bind="score" /></qg:hud>.

examples.intent: An action outside a handler

input.natural_language: Destroy the coins when the scene starts
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:destroy target="coin" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: An action runs when something happens: it goes inside a handler (qg:on-collision, qg:timer, q:if...).
examples.correction: Put it in a qg:timer after="1", or do not place the coins.

examples.intent: A name no q:set declared

input.natural_language: Add one to the score when a coin is touched
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:instance prefab="Coin" x="60" y="20" />
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18">
      <qg:on-collision with="coin">
        <q:set name="score" value="{score + 1}" />
      </qg:on-collision>
    </qg:character>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: 'score' is not declared: its first <q:set> reads it

examples.why_invalid: Every name is declared: there are no silent defaults.
examples.correction: Declare it first: <q:set name="score" value="0" type="number" /> in q:application (game state) or the scene.

examples.intent: A game with no scene

input.natural_language: A game that only declares its pictures
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
</q:application>

expected_error.message: a game needs at least one <qg:scene>

examples.why_invalid: The first scene is where the game starts.
examples.correction: Add <qg:scene name="main">...</qg:scene>.

examples.intent: Two scenes with the same name

input.natural_language: Two levels
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="level" />
  <qg:scene name="level" />
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: goto-scene and exits find a scene by its name.
examples.correction: Name them level-1 and level-2.

examples.intent: A function of the game setting a state no one declared

input.natural_language: A function the whole game can call, that resets the score
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <q:function name="reset"><q:set name="score" value="0" /></q:function>
  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

expected_error.message: 'score' is set and never read: a state of the game is declared with <q:set name="score" .../> in <q:application>

examples.why_invalid: No q:set declares score: in a function, a name no q:set of the game declares is a variable of the function, and one set and never read is a misspelt state.
examples.correction: Declare it in <q:application>: <q:set name="score" value="0" type="number" />.

examples.intent: A spawn with x but no y

input.natural_language: Spawn a coin at x 100
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:timer after="10">
      <qg:spawn prefab="Coin" x="100" />
    </qg:timer>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: A point needs both coordinates.
examples.correction: Write x="100" y="50", or at="me".

examples.intent: A set without a value in a handler

input.natural_language: Reset the score when jump is pressed
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <q:set name="score" value="0" type="number" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:on-input action="jump">
      <q:set name="score" />
    </qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: In a handler q:set assigns; the value is not optional.
examples.correction: Write <q:set name="score" value="0" />.

examples.intent: A tween that takes no time

input.natural_language: Move the door up instantly with a tween
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:on-input action="jump">
      <qg:tween target="me" property="y" to="10" seconds="0" />
    </qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: A tween eases over some seconds.
examples.correction: To move at once use <qg:put x= y= />; otherwise give seconds="0.5".

examples.intent: A deflect told both how to flip and where to go

input.natural_language: Bounce the ball off the paddle
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18">
      <qg:on-collision with="ball">
        <qg:deflect axis="x" dx="1" dy="0" />
      </qg:on-collision>
    </qg:character>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: axis=, or dx= and dy=, not both

examples.why_invalid: Flipping an axis and setting a heading are two different deflects.
examples.correction: Keep one: axis="x", or dx="1" dy="{random(-1, 1)}".

examples.intent: A velocity with no speed

input.natural_language: Stop the character
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:on-input action="jump">
      <qg:velocity target="me" />
    </qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: An axis not given keeps its speed, so a velocity with neither does nothing.
examples.correction: Write <qg:velocity target="hero" x="0" y="0" />.

examples.intent: A part that needs min= and max=

input.natural_language: An archer that keeps away from the player
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:prefab name="Archer" tag="archer" sheet="chars" hitbox="16x16" ai="behavior">
    <qg:behavior>
      <qg:keep-distance from="hero" />
    </qg:behavior>
  </qg:prefab>
  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: keep-distance keeps between min= and max= pixels: both are required.
examples.correction: Write <qg:keep-distance from="hero" min="50" max="90" />.

examples.intent: An item a prefab gives that was never declared

input.natural_language: A gem the player picks up
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:prefab name="Gem" tag="gem" sheet="tiles" frame="67" hitbox="12x12" gives="gem" />
  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: gives= names a qg:item, which says how many can be held and how it looks in the inventory.
examples.correction: Declare <qg:item name="gem" /> in q:application.

examples.intent: A tile kind that does not exist

input.natural_language: Lava tiles that hurt
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18">
    <qg:tile frame="68" kind="lava" />
  </qg:tileset>
  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

expected_error.message: kind="lava": must be one of ladder, water, ice, hurt

examples.why_invalid: The kinds are ladder, water, ice and hurt; what lava does is the game's own.
examples.correction: Use kind="hurt" and a qg:on-tile kind="hurt" on the character.

examples.intent: A q:if without its condition

input.natural_language: If the player has a key, open the door
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:on-input action="jump">
      <q:if><qg:pause /></q:if>
    </qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: q:if chooses by a condition.
examples.correction: Write <q:if condition="{held('key') > 0}">.

examples.intent: A handler for a tag nothing has

input.natural_language: When the hero touches a coin, add a point
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <q:set name="score" value="0" type="number" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="chars" x="20" y="20" hitbox="14x18">
      <qg:on-collision with="coin">
        <q:set name="score" value="{score + 1}" />
      </qg:on-collision>
    </qg:character>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: no prefab or zone has that tag

examples.why_invalid: with= names a tag of a prefab or a zone; a tag nothing carries is a typo or a missing prefab.
examples.correction: Declare <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" ... /> and place it with qg:instance.

examples.intent: An elseif after an inner q:if

input.natural_language: Dig a block (every fifth leaves a gem), or else put one back
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <q:set name="dug" value="0" type="number" />
    <qg:on-input action="jump">
      <q:if condition="{tile_at(1, 1) != 0}">
        <qg:set-tile col="1" row="1" tile="0" />
        <q:if condition="{dug % 5 == 0}">
          <qg:spawn prefab="Coin" at="me" />
        </q:if>
      <q:elseif condition="{dug > 0}">
        <qg:set-tile col="1" row="1" tile="23" />
      </q:elseif>
      </q:if>
    </qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: Right after an inner </q:if>, a q:elseif reads as the outer q:if's branch by nesting but looks like the inner one's: the parser refuses to guess (a QuantumParseError, before the game compiler).
examples.correction: Put the inner q:if before the other statements of its branch, or move the elseif inside the q:if it belongs to.

examples.intent: A state named like a property of every Godot node

input.natural_language: Keep the player's health as a number
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <q:set name="health" value="100" type="number" />
  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

expected_error.message: 'health' is a property of every Godot node

examples.why_invalid: Game and scene states become properties of Godot nodes; health, position, rotation, scale, visible and the like are taken.
examples.correction: Name it hp or energy.

examples.intent: Rollback for a scene that goes through physics

input.natural_language: Online co-op for the platformer, with rollback so it feels responsive
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:multiplayer players="2" rollback="8" />
  <qg:scene name="level">
    <qg:tilemap tileset="tiles" collision="true">
0,0,0
23,23,23
    </qg:tilemap>
    <qg:character id="p1" controller="platformer" player="1" sheet="chars" x="10" y="10" hitbox="14x18" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: rollback takes fighters, timers, menus, the HUD, pictures

examples.why_invalid: Rolling back re-runs ticks from a saved state; what goes through Godot's physics keeps no state to roll back.
examples.correction: Use plain lockstep: <qg:multiplayer players="2" delay="3" /> (no rollback=).

examples.intent: A loop name that is taken

input.natural_language: Damage every coin, naming each one other
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:timer after="1">
      <qg:for-each tag="coin" var="paused"><qg:damage target="paused" amount="1" /></qg:for-each>
    </qg:timer>
    <q:set name="paused" value="false" type="boolean" />
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: The name of each thing must not hide a state, a parameter or another loop variable.
examples.correction: Choose another name: var="coin".

examples.intent: Time stopped

input.natural_language: Freeze time with a time scale of zero
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:timer after="1"><qg:time-scale scale="0" /></qg:timer>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: scale= more than 0 and up to 4

examples.why_invalid: A game whose ticks never come stops for good; qg:pause is the way to stop a scene.
examples.correction: Use <qg:pause /> and <qg:resume />, or a small scale such as 0.1.

examples.intent: A screen handler of a scene without a tag

input.natural_language: Do something when anything leaves the screen
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:sound name="out" src="assets/kenney/audio/hurt.ogg" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:on-screen-exit><qg:play sound="out" /></qg:on-screen-exit>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: In a scene the handler is about the things of one tag; in a character or prefab it is about that one.
examples.correction: Write of="coin" (a prefab's tag), or put the handler in the prefab.

examples.intent: Fewer players than players

input.natural_language: A game for two that may start with two
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:multiplayer players="2" min-players="2" />
  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

expected_error.message: 2 or more, and fewer than players=

examples.why_invalid: min-players= says how many fewer may start; the same number is players= itself.
examples.correction: Leave min-players= out, or raise players=.

examples.intent: Statements straight inside a tween

input.natural_language: When the tween ends, add a point
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:prefab name="Coin" tag="coin" sheet="tiles" frame="151" hitbox="12x12" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <q:set name="points" value="0" type="number" />
    <qg:instance prefab="Coin" name="c" x="40" y="40" />
    <qg:timer after="1">
      <qg:tween target="c" property="y" to="20" seconds="0.5"><q:set name="points" value="{points + 1}" /></qg:tween>
    </qg:timer>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: holds one <qg:on-end> at most, and nothing else

examples.why_invalid: A tween runs over many ticks; what follows it runs when it is done, in its qg:on-end.
examples.correction: Wrap it: <qg:tween ...><qg:on-end><q:set .../></qg:on-end></qg:tween>.

examples.intent: A field the character does not have

input.natural_language: Show the hero's health
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="people" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <q:set name="shown" value="0" type="number" />
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="platformer" sheet="people" frame="0" x="40" y="40" hitbox="18x22" />
    <qg:timer every="10"><q:set name="shown" value="{hero.health}" /></qg:timer>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: hero.health: no such field; hero has facing, name, on_ceiling, on_floor, on_wall, player, state, x, y

examples.why_invalid: A platformer's character keeps no health (a fighter does): read before, hero.health stopped the game in Godot.
examples.correction: Keep the hearts in a q:set of the game, or use controller="fighter".

examples.intent: A delay with no count

input.natural_language: Later, end the level
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="people" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:scene name="main">
    <qg:on-input action="jump"><qg:after><qg:goto-scene name="main" /></qg:after></qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: <qg:after> takes ticks= or seconds=, one of them

examples.why_invalid: A delay needs to know how long it waits.
examples.correction: Write <qg:after seconds="2"> or <qg:after ticks="120">.

examples.intent: A function of the game reading a scene's state

input.natural_language: A function every room uses that reads the score of one room
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
  <qg:tileset name="tiles" src="assets/kenney/tilemap_packed.png" tile="18" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="people" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <q:function name="win" params="n"><q:set name="n" value="{points}" /></q:function>
  <qg:scene name="main"><q:set name="points" value="0" type="number" /></qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: A q:function of the game runs in every scene: it reads the game's state (q:set in q:application), its parameters and its own variables, not one scene's.
examples.correction: Declare points in <q:application>, or pass it: <q:call function="win" args="{points}" />.

examples.intent: A scene function named like one of the game

input.natural_language: Each room has its own hurt

<q:application id="bad" type="game">

  <qg:spritesheet name="people" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <q:function name="hurt"><qg:quit /></q:function>
  <qg:scene name="main"><q:function name="hurt"><qg:quit /></q:function></qg:scene>
</q:application>

expected_error.message: 'hurt' is a q:function of the game already

examples.why_invalid: Two functions of the same name in one scene: which runs would depend on nothing written.
examples.correction: Give the scene's another name.

examples.intent: Reading an action the game does not have

input.natural_language: Charge while dash is held

  <qg:spritesheet name="people" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />

    <qg:timer every="1"><q:if condition="{pressing('dash')}"><q:set name="charge" value="{charge + 1}" /></q:if></qg:timer>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>

examples.why_invalid: An action is a name the game declares (qg:input) or a default one: a misspelt one would read as never pressed.
examples.correction: Declare it: <qg:input action="dash" keys="Shift" />.

expected_error.message: heading= is for a prefab with ai="fly"

examples.why_invalid: Only a flying prefab goes along a heading; a coin stays where it is placed.
examples.correction: Give the prefab ai="fly" and a speed=, or spawn it without heading=.

examples.intent: A wall that would notice what touches it

input.natural_language: The wall says ouch when something touches it

<q:application id="bad" type="game">

  <qg:scene name="main" />
</q:application>

expected_error.message: a prefab that does not move: it would never run

examples.why_invalid: A prefab that does not move never touches anything itself; what moves into it does the touching.

examples.intent: Steering and walking at once

input.natural_language: A car that steers and also walks with the arrows
input.quantum_code:
<q:application id="bad" type="game">
